egress_proxy.py._Denied: Reject a malformed or disallowed CONNECT destination before establishing its upstream tunnel.
egress_proxy.py._Withdrawn: Stop tunnel work after the original proxy owner withdraws admission.
egress_proxy.py._hostname: Normalize one explicit DNS hostname and reject numeric, single-label or malformed destinations without resolving it.
egress_proxy.py.EgressPolicy: Bound exact DNS destinations, TLS port, live/total connection counts, transferred bytes and deadlines for one host-owned proxy.
egress_proxy.py.TunnelReceipt: Record the tunnel outcome and forwarded upload/download byte counts without claiming application success or TLS-content inspection.
egress_proxy.py._numeric_dial: Validate one public numeric IP, register its socket with the owner before a bounded connect, and close it on failure without another DNS lookup.
egress_proxy.py.EgressPolicy.__post_init__: Normalize and deduplicate the explicit host allowlist and reject unbounded, nonfinite or invalid capacities and deadlines.
egress_proxy.py.EgressPolicy.request_host: Require bounded ASCII CONNECT syntax, exact allowed DNS authority on port 443 and a matching Host header; do not inspect tunneled TLS.
egress_proxy.py.TunnelProxy.__init__: Configure one bounded worker pool and socket/byte accounting around injected resolver and dial functions; no listener is opened.
egress_proxy.py.TunnelProxy.submit: Take ownership of one connected stream, reserve live and total capacity, and return its worker future; rejected input is closed.
egress_proxy.py.TunnelProxy._check: Reject further tunnel progress once the original owner has withdrawn egress.
egress_proxy.py.TunnelProxy._admit: Track an upstream socket under the withdrawal lock or close it immediately if admission has ended.
egress_proxy.py.TunnelProxy.withdraw: Permanently reject new work and shut down all currently tracked sockets without waiting for worker receipts.
egress_proxy.py.TunnelProxy.close: Withdraw sockets, stop queued work and wait within the supplied budget; unfinished workers remain an explicit closure failure.
egress_proxy.py.TunnelProxy._header: Read a CONNECT header within the byte/deadline bound and return any already received tunnel tail without dropping its bytes.
egress_proxy.py.TunnelProxy._handle: Validate authority and all resolved IPs, dial one deterministic public address and forward opaque bytes; always release owned sockets and return a bounded outcome.
egress_proxy.py.TunnelProxy._pump: Forward both directions with bounded buffers, aggregate byte accounting, idle/wall deadlines and half-close propagation; counts measure sent payload bytes.
egress_proxy.py.TunnelProxy.submit.finished: Release settled worker capacity under the proxy lock without decrementing the total lifetime connection count.
egress_proxy.py.TunnelProxy._handle.admit: Retain an upstream socket for this tunnel cleanup before registering it against global proxy withdrawal.

egress_channel.py.EgressChannel: Own a private inherited descriptor channel and its receiver thread, forwarding accepted streams to the bounded host proxy without exposing a TCP listener.
egress_channel.py.EgressChannel.__init__: Create the private sequenced socketpair and start its descriptor receiver; this host setup does not spawn a native actor.
egress_channel.py.EgressChannel.close_child_end: Close only the host copy of the child endpoint after spawn; separately duplicated pinned descriptors remain their callers' responsibility.
egress_channel.py.EgressChannel.withdraw: Withdraw proxy work and close both retained channel ends, waking the descriptor receiver without waiting for its final receipt.
egress_channel.py.EgressChannel.close: Withdraw the channel, bound receiver/proxy shutdown by one deadline and fail if the receiver thread remains alive.
egress_channel.py.EgressChannel._receive: Accept exactly one FD per typed private frame within the lifetime budget, close malformed/unclaimed descriptors and withdraw on channel loss without logging raw frames.

native_network.py._validate: Validate numeric resolver directives or a parseable public-certificate PEM bundle; these inputs enable DNS/TLS and do not restrict destinations.
native_network.py.PublicNetworkFile: Fingerprint one host-selected public resolver or CA asset by path, physical identity and exact content for later sealed mounting.
native_network.py.NativeNetwork: Pair explicitly inspected resolver and public CA manifests; the pair supplies network inputs rather than credentials or destination authority.
native_network.py.PublicNetworkFile._read: Read and validate a trusted bounded regular file while checking descriptor metadata and path identity, returning its manifest and exact bytes.
native_network.py.PublicNetworkFile.inspect: Inspect a selected existing resolver or CA file without retaining its descriptor, sanitizing unavailable or invalid source errors.
native_network.py.NativeNetwork.inspect: Inspect both host-selected public network assets without opening a network connection or creating native state.

peer_process.py.boot_id: Read the current Linux boot identity used to reject recovery against a different kernel lifetime.
peer_process.py.observer_namespace: Read the current observer PID-namespace inode so recovery can reject a changed observation domain.
peer_process.py.start_ticks: Read a process start time from procfs while accounting for spaces and closing parentheses in its command name; this alone does not pin its identity.
peer_process.py._libc: Configure libc pidfd entry points for descriptor-based process observation and signaling.
peer_process.py._pidfd: Open a kernel handle for the currently observed process or expose the actual errno; a numeric PID alone is never used for signaling.
peer_process.py._signal: Send SIGKILL only through the pinned pidfd, accepting an already absent target and propagating other kernel failures.
peer_process.py._init_fields: Read start ticks, PID-namespace inode and namespace-init status from procfs; the caller must pin and validate the surrounding observation.
peer_process.py.NamespaceIdentity: Retain the originally captured private namespace-init and observer identities for later pidfd-based closure checks.
peer_process.py.NamespaceIdentity.capture: Pin a live reported PID, require private namespace-init identity and optional launcher parent, then capture recovery metadata before payload release.
peer_process.py.NamespaceIdentity.from_record: Reconstruct only declared identity fields from an existing record; this conversion does not recapture or validate a live process.

recovery.py.RunRecovery.__init__: Bind recovery to the existing run store and its peer registry without discovering or starting replacement actors.
recovery.py.RunRecovery.inspection: Return bounded current peer/job/effect evidence and protocol/origin blockers for owner recovery without retiring actors or replaying effects.
recovery.py.RunRecovery._intent: Validate the explicit recovery command and build the attempt/fence-bound intent used to compare durable operation receipts.
recovery.py.RunRecovery._protocol: Require the original recoverable native/business peer protocol and validate each stored origin before allowing recovery work.
recovery.py.RunRecovery.begin: Persist one original recovery intent, withdraw run authority and return scoped peer/grant identities, or recover its existing completion receipt.
recovery.py.RunRecovery.complete: Require matching recovery intent and closed-peer proof before retiring the attempt and storing its receipt/event; never start inference or accept the task.
recovery.py.RunRecovery.reconcile: Recover an existing receipt or retire each originally registered peer and complete the same recovery intent without replaying business work.
